chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: His first recording date: the 1947 Los Angeles session with Witherspoon
summary: Tate leads his first date before the recording ban, with C.Q. Price singing blues, Jimmy Witherspoon, and the Supreme label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Tell me about the session you did in '47 with the jump band in Los Angeles. You had Jimmy Witherspoon and Chico Hamilton.
Oh, that band?
Yeah.
That was the first -- that was my first recording date. It was just before --
You were still with Basie.
Still with Basie. And it was just before that record ban.
Right.

You know, they had a record ban for two years. Oh, and I had C.Q. Price and Emmett Berry, Ted Donnelly, Chico and a very good guitarist by the name of Louis Springer. I didn't find out where he was until -- what's the boy that
Uh-huh, yeah.

I mean, Jack Sheldon told me. But the way that came about, well, I was trying to get a record date, you know, I had been trying and this cat wanted to record me when we got to California. So we got to California, he says, "Well, now's the time and we'll do it just before, you know, before the record band." And that's the way it was. C.Q. -- Rush was going to sing the blues. C.Q. Price sang the blues with it, the first time he'd ever sang the blues.

So Rush -- we had Rush. Rush was going to be on my date. Shit, Rush talked to them, man, Rush wanted more money than all the band was going to get. So C.Q. got mad, he said, "Man, fuck Rush. Shit, I sing the goddamn blues. We going to do this record date. To hell with Rush." So that's why he sang the blues. So we did it without -- you know, without Jimmy.
How did Witherspoon get in there?

Well, this was his first thing, too. So the man said, "Well, I got a blues singer, too," says, "and I want you all to back him." So we did a thing called "Six Foot-Two Baby" or something with Spoon. That was one of Spoon's first dates, too. And they brought him in, the record people. And then C.Q. sang, you know, like because Spoon wanted to do his thing, you know, and of course, we played for him. Then

they gave me a big band. Their records didn't get out much. I had it and I don't know whatever -- had a vocal, choral group, sang beautiful harmony. They had the right kind of harmony and I had about 12-piece band and I only had one record and I don't know, it's got lost.
(Laughter.)
I don't know where -- with Preston Love playing first and -- beautiful sounding band.
Did the record sell at all?
That one out on the West Coast did. Yeah, that one, it sold quite a bit. Had some nice royalties off of that. And he died, he was really a nice guy. He --
Who was that?
His name was Al Patrick.
And the label was?
Supreme. But they sold it to -- they sold the masters to Alun---
Morgan.

Yeah, in London. And he's got the black Lion, uh-huh. That's -- but it was originally on Supreme. Now, their biggest hit was from a girl by the name of Paula Watson. She made a record called 'The Little Bird Told Me.' They sold a million copies with her. And Vic did some things for them, but the biggest thing, their biggest record, was with Paula.
